title: Projected cost of the recursive learner
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let a node finder for $k$-juntas on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube be given, and let $f$ be a Boolean function on that cube taking values in $\{\pm1\}$. Fix a learning parameter $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2]$, an additive map $q$ from learning costs to nonnegative integers with $q(0)=0$, and a nonnegative integer $B$. Suppose every outcome in the support of each node-finder call, for every set $P$ of fixed coordinates and every assignment of signs on $P$, has projected cost at most $B$. Then for every recursion fuel $r$, every such $P$ and assignment, and every outcome in the support of the recursive learner, its projected cost is at most $T(r)B$, where $T(0)=1$ and $T(r+1)=1+2T(r)$.
